sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)
- ls: List directory contents
- obsidian: Run an Obsidian CLI command on the vault
- web_enable: If tools for web search, source checking, content fetching, stored-result retrieval are not already available, call web_enable first whenever current, external, or linked information could help; the tools appear on the next model request.

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use obsidian—not bash, read, write, edit, ls, find, or grep—for every operation on files in an Obsidian vault; pass vault=<name> if it is not the focused vault.
- Format: `<command> <key=value> ... <flag>`
- Quote spaces: `file="My Note"`, content=`# Title`.
- content_from=SourceNoteName to clone an existing note's content.
- eval file=ScriptNoteName for JS from vault note.
- format=json for structured output (search, tasks, tags).
- Boolean flags: permanent, overwrite, total, verbose, inline, silent.
- file= for wikilinks, path= for exact paths.
- Commands: read, create, write, append, prepend, delete, move, rename,
- search, tags, tag-rename, property:set, property:rename, properties,
- tasks, task-create, create-from-template,
- backlinks, outline, links, daily:*,
- vault, files, history, diff, templates, eval, bookmarks, plugins,
- frontmatter:wrap.
- move: `destination=<path>` accepted as alias for `to=<path>`.
- Search with replace: `search query=text replace=new regex=true preview=true`
- Files by missing property: `files missing-property=created`
- Property rename: `property:rename from=date to=created`
- Frontmatter wrap: `frontmatter:wrap`
- property:set for lists (tags, aliases): name=tags type=list value="#tag1,#tag2" file=Note
- search --replace uses preview=true for dry-run; omit to apply.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

Project-specific instructions and guidelines:

<project_instructions path="D:\Agent-Harness\agent-harness_omni\agent-harness\AGENTS.md">
# Pi Analysis Project Guidance

## Scope

This workspace contains the existing Python agent harness. Pi should be treated as the primary general-purpose agent runtime; do not recreate its agent loop, LLM client, or basic filesystem tools inside this repository.

## Operating rules

- Use Pi's built-in `read`, `bash`, `grep`, `find`, and `ls` capabilities for analysis.
- Use the skills in the user `.agents/skills` directory for file, log, CSV, JSON, and report workflows.
- Prefer bounded searches and parsers over loading large files into the model context.
- Keep credentials, tokens, and personal data out of reports and logs.
- Record durable project decisions in `memory/`; do not add a vector database without a concrete retrieval requirement.

## Planned connectors

Database, Splunk, and external API connectors are intentionally deferred until the local file and shell workflow is verified. Add them as focused Pi extensions with explicit read-only or confirmation boundaries.

</project_instructions>
</project_context>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: grep
toolsAdded.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

toolsAdded.name: find
toolsAdded.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

toolsAdded.name: ls
toolsAdded.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

# Roadmap

Working document for F-006 post-reversal work. Sourced from `docs/F006_LEDGER.md`
and the operator rulings of 2026-10-01.

## Status

Branch `fix/f006-policy-deny-not-fatal` is merged into `origin/main` at `fca77fc`
(merge commit `066b2b4`, `gate recovery depth on non-CONTINUE strategies`).

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `platform/pi` | 336 pass / 0 fail |
| `platform/core` | 189 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped |
| `platform/*.test.mjs` | 22 pass / 0 fail |

## Operator rulings, 2026-10-01

**R1 — the D1 contract reversal.** A denied call is a **result, not a death**.
`POLICY_DENIED` returns `CONTINUE` / `POLICY_SOFT_REFUSED` at every violation label
and at every budget. Rationale: a refusal is an answer, not a fault, and a fault is
what a task is allowed to die of. `abort` still ends a task, one layer out, in
`precheckToolCall` → `abortTask`, where it is reachable.

**R2 — `REPLANNING` stays an open question.** See "Human decision required".

**R3 — the ledger gets a reversal entry.** `docs/F006_LEDGER.md` §2.5 quotes
pre-reversal code as present tense. It is evidence of a bug, not current law, and
must be marked as such before the ledger is used as a corrective authority again.

## Human decision required

**`REPLANNING` and the stored-failure echo** — ledger §3.2.

`REFUSED_EXECUTION_STATES` includes `REPLANNING`, which the ledger's own
`TERMINAL_TASK_STATES` comment calls "still live and still owned by whoever started
it". Of the three sites gated on that set, only `kernel-adapter.ts:835`
(`describeTerminalRefusal`) replays the stored reason. **That replay is unpinned for
`REPLANNING`.**

Two candidate answers, both live:

- **yes** — a live `REPLANNING` task should replay a stored reason, and the pin
  should be added;
- **no** — `REPLANNING` should refuse without replaying a stored reason.

**Deliberately not pinned.** A pin must assert one of these, and choosing silently
would launder an open design question into settled law. Requires an operator
decision. No code change.

## P1 — caller-boundary fix: a refusal is indistinguishable from a tool fault

Measured on `fca77fc`. `recordToolResult` returns to its caller:

```json
{"status":"INVALID","validator":"pi-result","message":"policy denied: refused by rule X"}
```

The reason reaches the caller verbatim, so attribution is intact. But
`validator: "pi-result"` with `status: "INVALID"` is **byte-identical to a genuine
tool failure**. Any caller branching on `validator` to decide whether to retry
treats a policy refusal as a fault and retries it — the D1 defect reborn one layer
out, at the return boundary, where the kernel's own `POLICY_DENIED` classification
can no longer reach in to correct it.

This is a behaviour change at a **public boundary**. It gets its own review cycle
and is not bundled with the reversal.

Documenting pin: `platform/pi/f006-policy-denied.test.ts`, `D1.1c`. It asserts the
preconditions (the refusal is classified `POLICY_DENIED` internally, and the reason
reaches the caller verbatim) and names the gap in a comment. **It does not assert
`validator` is undefined** — a permanently red pin breaks CI and trains people to
ignore red. The pin inverts when the fix lands.

## Phase 5 split — operator ruling, effective immediately

Phase 5 previously ran as one gated item. It is now split:

- **5a — scaffolding. AUTHORIZED. Track B, new branch `docker-ui-scaffold`.**
  Dockerfile + compose for the green baseline, and a frontend shell built on
  mock data. Contracts only; no dependency on any unbuilt plane. Track B
  commits directly to its own branch, MR per milestone, operator merge
  ratifies. **Track B must not modify `platform/` internals.**
- **5b — production integration. STILL GATED** on the acceptance test. Not
  un-gated by this ruling.

The two tracks, and the only things gating production integration:

- **Track A (unchanged, continues here):** Phase 1 queue → State plane →
  Observability plane.
- **Track B (scaffold only):** 5a above.

Track A items are the only gate on production integration.

**Phase numbering is externally sourced.** Neither `roadmap.md` nor
`docs/F006_LEDGER.md` contained a `Phase N` construct before this entry; the
numbering comes from a plan held outside this repository. Recorded as stated, not
reconstructed.

**5a's own gate is stated and currently UNVERIFIED:** the container must run the
full test suite green before any UI work. Docker is not installed in the authoring
environment, so the gate cannot be evaluated there. See Track B item 1 below.

**Track B forks from `12c89d5`,** not `fca77fc`. The delta is docs and one comment;
both are green, and forking from the tip avoids a rebase later. Fork SHA recorded
in the MR.

## Standing rules

**No agent may claim verified-green for a gate this harness cannot execute.**
Label the result `UNVERIFIED`, name the executor who must run it, and move on.
Ratified 2026-10-01 after Track B's container gate was found to be unrunnable here.

The rationale is not ceremony. An agent-authored "verified green" for an
environment it never started is the same defect as a caller told `pi-result` for a
policy refusal: a truthful-looking value that is not what it claims to be, sitting
exactly where a later reader will not re-check it. `UNVERIFIED` plus a named
executor is cheap. A fabricated green is not.

## Track B interface ownership

All Track B wire-point interfaces are marked **`@provisional`** in code, with a
comment naming the owning plane (State / Observability).

**Track A is not bound by them.** If Track A's real contracts diverge, **Track B
updates to match — never the reverse.** Track B may not constrain Track A's
design; these interfaces are scaffolding, not a contract.

## Remaining work

| # | Item | State |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | This roadmap | done |
| 2 | Stale comment, `kernel-adapter.ts:1620-1623` | done (`d25ee8e`) |
| 3 | Documenting pin D1.1c | **blocked — awaiting operator paste** |
| 4 | Ledger reversal entry | pending, diff first |
| 5 | Caller-boundary fix (validator threading) | deferred — own review cycle |
| B1 | Dockerfile + compose, green baseline | in progress |
| B2 | Frontend shell, mock data | pending B1 |
| B3 | Typed wire points for State + Observability | pending B2 |

## Standing hazards

- **The §3 alarm is disarmed.** Its trigger — a denial certificate reading
  `TOOL_FAILURE` and dying of `REPLAN_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` — is now unreachable: a
  denial returns `CONTINUE` under every label at every budget. An operator reading
  §3 believes they are covered and are not. Corrected by the ledger reversal entry.
- **`docs/F006_LEDGER.md` is not a specification.** It is an incident record. Using
  it to justify a code change, without first reading the section's framing, will
  revert the reversal.

## The deletion guard: shell must not bypass deletion control

**The rule.** A command that invokes a destructive program is denied at every
tool tier, whatever flags it carries: `rm`, `rm -f`, `rm -rf`, `rm -r -f`,
`rm -fr`, and plain `rm file` are all the same decision. The same holds for
`rmdir`, `del`, `erase`, `unlink`, `shred`, and `Remove-Item`.

**Why it is a rule and not an accident.** `bash` is a *permitted* tool, and the
Pi integration has no separate denied delete tool. A deletion performed through
the shell is therefore reachable no matter which tool names it, so the only
place it can be stopped is the command itself. An earlier version relied on the
substring `rm -rf`, which happened to also catch `rm -f` — correct by luck, and
blind to plain `rm file`. The guard is now expressed as **whole-token matching**
in `destructiveCommandTokens`, so it is complete by construction and a word that
merely contains a program name is not caught by accident (`echo charm` and
`node confirm.js` are allowed).

**Scope boundary.** The guard, like the other command-scope rules, applies to
command text only. A write whose payload merely *contains* the string `rm -rf`
is **allowed**, because documenting a command in a runbook or a report is not
running it. Injected content is still caught, because it arrives inside command
text: `bash -c "rm -rf /"` and `echo "rm -rf x" | sh` are both denied.

**Scratch cleanup.** When this guard refuses a deletion, the correct response is
to **overwrite or leave the file, never to delete it**. This is not a
theoretical restriction: it is why the report-writer skill writes to a new path
rather than clearing an old one, and why the log-analysis skill never tidies up
after itself. If a task genuinely cannot proceed without a deletion, that is a
signal that the workflow needs redesigning, not that the guard should be
loosened.

**Guardrail, not a sandbox.** This list cannot constrain what an already-permitted
command does, cannot prevent a deletion performed by a program that reads a
script, and is not a substitute for OS-level isolation. Path allowlisting,
secret isolation, and OS-level sandboxing remain deferred work; see
`docs/SECURITY.md`. Treat this list as a cheap, high-value tripwire, not as the
security boundary itself.

Measured against `fix/f006-post-reversal-ledger` @ **`28800c2`**, `docker-ui-scaffold` @ **`8fd1d5b`**, `main`/`origin/main` @ **`fca77fc`**. Suite at `28800c2`: **534 tests, 532 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped** (`npm test`, typecheck included). GREEN on the host.

---

### 1. Operator blockers — restated, tree-verified

| # | Blocker | Verdict, measured |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Push pending** | **CONFIRMED.** `fix/f006-post-reversal-ledger` is 3 ahead / 0 behind `origin` — `1e85d54`, `3e83998`, `28800c2` are local only. |
| 2 | **Restart pending — blocks C2** | **CONFIRMED.** No restart confirmation exists in `docs/MANIFEST.md`; the manifest still reads "Restart is still pending" (line 216). C2 cannot start. |

| 4 | **Docker gate run on B1** | **OUTSTANDING — and the gate cannot go green as authored.** See finding 4.2. |
| 5 | **NEW — Track B branch is local-only** | `docker-ui-scaffold` exists on no remote: `git ls-remote --heads origin` returns 0 matches, and no remote branch contains `8fd1d5b`. The MR per milestone cannot be opened until it is pushed. |

### 2. C1 — echoed refusal: **CLOSED**, and the closure is pinned, not asserted

Closed by reading the source and measuring, committed as `1e85d54` + `3e83998`, pinned green in `platform/pi/c1-replanning-stored-failure.test.ts` (`C1.1`–`C1.4`).

The question had no live answer to give. `failureReason` has one writer (`KernelAdapter.advance`, `platform/pi/kernel-adapter.ts:589`) and all eight call sites pair it with `advance("FAILED", …)`; `FAILED` is terminal and cannot revive. `REPLANNING` is entered at `:1397` and left at `:1398` on consecutive statements with no `await`, and `advance` emits nothing — so no code can observe the state at all. The replay tail is unreachable, and neither candidate answer was chosen. `C1.3` guards the terminal replay, so the closure cannot later be satisfied by deleting the attribution.

Two defects fell out and are filed in `docs/F006_LEDGER.md` §5:

- **Item 8 — a refusal that settles as a *sibling* kills the task. Live, reachable, unfixed.** I confirmed the path in source: `platform/pi/kernel-adapter.ts:1295` sets `attemptBlocked = true` for any `INVALID` validation, **before** the sibling early return at `:1300`, so the D1 `CONTINUE` branch at `:1310+` never runs and `denialReason` is never read. The last sibling succeeds, `lastValidation` is `VALID`, and `finishTask` fails the task on `attemptBlocked` with a reason naming no rule and no policy — while nothing actually failed verification.
- **Item 9 — the `REPLANNING` refusal text tells a live task that it terminated** (`:795`). One sentence. Deferred: it changes a public refusal string.

### 3. Stash disposition — ruling verified, and it holds

`927fdb1e` **does** contain the dropped stash's content. Verified tree-first from the dangling object the drop left behind:

- dropped stash = **`1a9b271`** `"On docker-ui-scaffold: task4 ledger reversal entry (belongs to Track A)"` (base `651cf61` @ `12c89d5`)

- nothing unique was destroyed; the drop was legitimate and had already happened before this session

**`stash@{1}` does not exist.** `git stash list` returns exactly one entry — `stash@{0}: part-c-unrequested-2026-09-30` (`17cab62`) — because the ledger-reversal stash was dropped and the part-C one shifted down. It is **untouched and recorded as inherited state** in `docs/MANIFEST.md`, as ruled. Its content is superseded (the strategy-fund work is in HEAD's `platform/core/recovery.ts`), with one element not carried over — `ConfiguredPolicy.lastFailureSignature`, replaced by the adapter-side `lastAttemptSignature`. Left intact for your disposition, as instructed.

### 4. Track B item 1 — authored, and it has a defect that blocks its own gate

`8fd1d5b` on `docker-ui-scaffold` (forked from `12c89d5`, per ruling) adds `Dockerfile` (39 lines) and `docker-compose.yml` (32). It is correctly labelled `UNVERIFIED` with you named as executor and the gate command in both files. It touches no `platform/` internals. The frontend shell scaffold was **not** started.

**4.2 The container suite will fail, and not on a test defect.** The image copies `platform`, `docs`, `tsconfig.json` and `package*.json`. The suite also reads repo-relative paths it never copies:

| Missing from image | Required by |
|---|---|
| `.pi/neurofebric-policy.json` | `platform/pi/policy-port.test.ts:541` — asserts the file "must exist and parse" |

| `reports/` | `platform/pi/write-approval.test.ts:156` (write target) |

Additionally `tsconfig.json` sets `"include": ["platform/**/*.ts", ".pi/extensions/*.ts"]`, so without `.pi/` the container's typecheck silently covers **less** than the host's — a green that would mean less than the gate claims. Three `COPY --chown=node:node .pi ./.pi`, `skills`, `reports` lines close all four.
